Best-of-N scores every proposal on the {term.splitVal} set, so it is capped at {val_count} {term.examplePlural} to keep each proposal affordable; {test_count} are held out as {term.splitTest}, and the remaining {train_count} stay in {term.splitTrain}, which Best-of-N doesn't use.
submit.split.rationale.best_of_n.holdout: Best-of-N never trains — it scores every proposal on the {term.splitVal} set — so {val_count} {term.examplePlural} go to {term.splitVal} and {test_count} are held out as {term.splitTest} to check the winner.
submit.split.rationale.best_of_n.pooled: This dataset is very small ({total} {term.examplePlural}). Best-of-N never trains — it scores every proposal on a single set — so all {term.examplePlural} go into that set, which also serves as the holdout.
submit.split.rationale.large: This is a large dataset ({total} {term.examplePlural}). {val_count} {term.examplePlural} go to {term.splitVal} and {test_count} to {term.splitTest}; once the dataset reaches these caps they keep {term.optimization} time reasonable without evaluating on more {term.examplePlural} than needed.
submit.split.rationale.medium: This is a medium-sized dataset ({total} {term.examplePlural}). A 60/20/20 split leaves enough {term.examplePlural} for all three sets.
submit.split.rationale.meta_harness.hold: Meta-Harness runs the agent on {term.splitTrain} and {term.splitVal} cases alike, so they are pooled: {train_count} {term.examplePlural} drive the {term.optimization} and {test_count} are held out as {term.splitTest} to check the winner.
submit.split.rationale.meta_harness.pool: This dataset is very small ({total} {term.examplePlural}). Meta-Harness runs the agent on {term.splitTrain} and {term.splitVal} cases alike, so all {term.examplePlural} go into one pool, which also serves as the holdout.
submit.split.rationale.small: This dataset is small ({total} {term.examplePlural}). 80% goes to {term.splitTrain} and 20% to {term.splitVal} to give GEPA a separate evaluation set; there aren't enough {term.examplePlural} for a {term.splitTest} set too.
submit.split.rationale.tiny: This dataset is very small ({total} {term.examplePlural}). There aren't enough {term.examplePlural} for a separate {term.splitVal} or {term.splitTest} set, so GEPA reuses the same examples for both {term.splitTrain} and evaluation during {term.optimization}.

tooltip.data.shuffle_explanation: Shuffles the order of rows before the split, so the file order does not accidentally affect the results

tooltip.data.split.train: Examples the optimizer uses to build prompt candidates
tooltip.data.split.val: Examples that rank the candidates during optimization
tooltip.data.split_explanation: The dataset is split into three parts: train for learning, val for choosing the prompt, and test for the final measurement
tooltip.flex.optimized_code: The program code GEPA rewrote alongside the prompt for this Flex optimization — the optimized Python that runs in the serve sandbox
tooltip.grid.avg_response_time_per_pair: Average duration per language model call, by model pair
tooltip.grid.best_pair_default: Default: the pair with the highest quality score. You can switch to any other pair.
tooltip.grid.generation_models: The models that produce answers. Each pair in the grid search uses a different task model
tooltip.grid.quality_speed_combined: Quality and speed for each model pair, side by side. The higher the quality and speed, the better the pair.
tooltip.grid.reflection_models: The models that analyze errors and suggest improvements. Each pair uses a different optimization model
tooltip.grid.score_comparison: Comparison of the baseline score and the optimized score for each model pair
tooltip.lm_activity.cell.avg_ms: The average time per call in this stage
tooltip.lm_activity.cell.calls: The number of calls made in this stage
tooltip.lm_activity.column.generation: Calls made to the task model — the model that produces answers
tooltip.lm_activity.column.reflection: Calls made to the optimization model — the model that analyzes errors and suggests improvements
tooltip.lm_activity.section: Language model activity by stage — how many calls were made and how long they took, for the task and optimization models separately
tooltip.lm_activity.stage.baseline: Calls made while measuring the baseline score — before the optimizer started working
tooltip.lm_activity.stage.evaluation: Calls made while measuring the optimized score — after the optimization finished
tooltip.lm_activity.stage.training: Calls made during the optimization itself — while the optimizer built prompt candidates
tooltip.lm_activity.total_row: Total calls and average time across all stages
tooltip.model.generation: The model that actually produces the answer during the optimization
tooltip.model.reflection: The model that checks mistakes and suggests how to improve the instructions during optimization
tooltip.model_config.base_url: The address of your own OpenAI-compatible server — Ollama, vLLM, LM Studio or an enterprise gateway. Leave empty to use the provider's default server
tooltip.model_config.max_tokens: The maximum prediction length — a token is roughly one word
tooltip.model_config.model: The model that will run the optimization. Choose from the model catalog, or a custom model discovered from the Base URL
tooltip.model_config.temperature: How creative the model is — a low value gives consistent answers, a high one more varied
tooltip.module.choice: A DSPy module is a component in the program that calls a language model: it wraps each signature in a prompting technique and defines the structure of the call to the model in order to produce the output defined in the signature. Within this framework, the optimizer tunes the module's learnable parameters, such as instructions and examples in the prompt
tooltip.module.cot: Chain of Thought — adds a reasoning field that leads the model to think step-by-step before the final answer; usually improves accuracy on complex tasks
tooltip.module.flex: Flex — the optimizer rewrites the program's code and prompt together, then runs the generated Python in a sandbox; best for tasks that need real computation, not just a single model call
tooltip.module.predict: Predict — the basic module: maps the input to the output in a single call to the model, with no intermediate steps
tooltip.module.react: ReAct — an agent that combines reasoning with tool calls in a loop until it produces the output defined by the Signature
tooltip.module.workflow: Workflow — a graph of several steps: Signatures, Python code, and tools wired together on a visual canvas. Optimization improves the instructions of all steps together, against one metric on the final output
tooltip.optimizer.choice: The method that tries to improve the prompt and find a version with a higher score
tooltip.react.auth: Authentication header (Authorization header) for the MCP server. Not stored on the server and not exposed to the chat agent
tooltip.react.mcp_url: The address of the MCP server from which the agent's tools are loaded
tooltip.react.optimized_tools: The tools the agent (ReAct) runs in a loop, with the descriptions and arguments the optimizer refined during optimization
tooltip.react.tool_source: Where the tool list is loaded from: a live MCP server, or a snapshot of tools from the dataset
tooltip.score.baseline: Baseline score before optimization: how the program did without an improved prompt or selected examples
tooltip.score.improvement: The gap between the optimized score and the baseline score. The larger it is, the more the optimization improved the result
tooltip.score.logged_metrics: Scores your metric recorded with log_metrics — e.g. precision and recall — averaged over the test set, before and after optimization
tooltip.score.optimized: Optimized score after optimization: how the program did with the chosen prompt and examples
tooltip.score.progression: How the score changed from attempt to attempt while the optimizer searched for a better prompt
tooltip.serve.api_url_react: The API URL you send a POST request to with the user message; the optimized ReAct agent's response is streamed back over SSE
tooltip.serve.api_url_run: The API URL you send POST requests to with the input fields in order to get a prediction from the improved program
tooltip.serve.section_pair: API URL and code snippets to integrate the selected pair into your app
tooltip.serve.section_run: API URL and code snippets to integrate the improved program into your app
tooltip.submit.depth: How wide GEPA's search is: light runs fast with fewer attempts; deeper checks more options and takes more time
tooltip.submit.eval_rounds: How many times to run a full evaluation to check prompt candidates
tooltip.submit.merge: When enabled, GEPA can merge and combine ideas from several good candidates into one prompt
tooltip.submit.metric_calls: Total metric calls (rollouts) the entire optimization may spend — the budget unit used in the GEPA paper. Setting it overrides evaluation rounds; choosing a search depth overrides both
tooltip.submit.pxn_parents: How many different candidates to improve each round. Higher explores more directions in parallel, at higher cost
tooltip.submit.pxn_proposals: How many rewrites to draw from each candidate. p×n candidates are evaluated per round, batched together
tooltip.submit.reflection_minibatch: How many examples the model checks in each feedback round to find error patterns
tooltip.submit.target_score: Stop the search once validation reaches this percentage; leave it empty to use the full search budget
tooltip.submit.name: A short name that identifies this {term.optimization} in the list and in comparisons — say what you're trying to improve
tooltip.submit.description: Free-text notes on what this optimization is trying to achieve; shown in its details so the context isn't lost
tooltip.submit.privacy: Private keeps the optimization out of public search; public lets anyone find it and browse the results
tooltip.submit.optimization_type: A single {term.optimizationTypeRun} uses one model pair; a {term.optimizationTypeGrid} repeats it for every task × optimization model combination and compares them
tooltip.submit.column_roles: Input is what the {term.program} receives for each example, output is the expected answer the {term.metric} compares against, and ignored columns stay out of the optimization
tooltip.submit.models: The models that take part in the optimization: the {term.generationModel} answers the examples, and the optional {term.reflectionModel} reviews mistakes and rewrites the instructions
tooltip.submit.generation_models: Every task model picked here is paired with every optimization model — the number of optimizations is the product of the two lists
tooltip.submit.reflection_models: The models that review mistakes and propose better instructions; each one is paired with every task model in the list
tooltip.submit.optimizer_params: The settings handed to the {term.optimizer} that control how wide, how long and how expensive the search is
tooltip.submit.react_section: Where the ReAct agent gets its tools and how it connects to them; applies only when the {term.module} is a ReAct agent
tooltip.submit.dataset_file: The uploaded file — every row is one example the optimization learns from or is measured on
tooltip.submit.dataset_size: How many rows and columns were detected in the file; the rows are shared out between train, validation and test
tooltip.submit.total_pairs: How many optimizations the grid search launches: every task model × every optimization model
tooltip.submit.estimate: The expected cost range for this optimization based on the chosen models and {term.dataset} size; the actual charge depends on how many calls the {term.optimizer} makes. With your own provider key only the platform fee is shown
tooltip.submit.cost_ceiling: A hard cap on what this optimization may spend — once its accumulated charge would exceed the ceiling, it stops instead of spending more
tooltip.submit.blackbox.seed: Where the search starts: every new version is a rewrite of this. Leave it empty to let the engine start from scratch
tooltip.submit.blackbox.objective: In a sentence or two, what counts as better. The engine reads this every time it proposes a rewrite
tooltip.submit.blackbox.background: Context that helps the engine understand the domain — audience, constraints, style; it shapes the proposals but not the score
tooltip.submit.blackbox.proposer: The coding agent that writes and revises candidates inside the sandbox — any installed harness can drive the engine
tooltip.submit.blackbox.proposer_candida: How many candidate variants Meta-Harness asks the agent for in each iteration (1–8)
tooltip.submit.blackbox.proposer_max_too: The most tool calls (reading, searching and editing files, running commands) the coding agent may make while writing one candidate (1–1000). A lower cap keeps each candidate cheaper; a higher one leaves room for larger changes.
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.title: Advanced search settings for ShinkaEvolve. Every field starts at the engine's default, so you can leave this closed.
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.editor: Single model call: the optimization model returns each new version in one response, as a diff, a full rewrite or a crossover. Coding agent (Pi): the Pi agent reads, searches and edits the code with tools to make each new version.
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.num_islan: How many separate populations evolve in parallel (1–8). More islands keep more diverse ideas alive.
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.migration: How many versions pass between migrations, when islands share their best versions (1–100).
Share of each island's versions copied to another island at each migration (0–1). 0 keeps the islands apart.
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.parent_se: How ShinkaEvolve picks the version to edit next.
Favors higher-scoring versions while still giving rarely tried ones a chance.
Ranks the versions and picks from the top far more often; tune it with alpha and the exploitation ratio.
Keeps editing a fixed set of the best versions.
How strongly weighted selection favors high scores (0.1–100). Higher values pick the leaders more often.
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.exploitat: Steepness of the power-law ranking (0–10). Higher values concentrate on the top versions.
Share of picks that come from the best versions rather than the wider archive (0–1).
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.num_beams: How many top versions beam search keeps editing (1–20).
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.patch_dif: Share of changes that edit parts of a version in place.
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.patch_ful: Share of changes that rewrite the whole version.
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.patch_cro: Share of changes that combine two versions.
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.max_patch: How many times a model may retry a change that failed to apply (1–10).
How many times a new parent is drawn when a change keeps failing (1–10).
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.archive_s: How many strong versions the archive keeps as parents and inspiration (1–500).
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.num_archi: How many archive versions the model sees as examples with each change (0–10).
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.num_top_k: How many of the best versions the model sees as examples with each change (0–10).
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.elite_sel: Share of the archive reserved for the highest-scoring versions (0–1).
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.use_text_: Include the scorer's written feedback in the model's prompts, not just the score.
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.novelty: Skip versions that are near copies of existing ones. Uses embeddings and a model check, which adds calls. Off by default.
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.code_embe: How similar two versions may be before the newer one counts as a duplicate (0.5–1). Lower values reject more.
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.max_novel: How many times to retry a change rejected as a duplicate (1–10).
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.meta_note: Every so often, sum up what worked as tips for later changes, using the first optimization model. On by default.
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.meta_rec_: How many versions pass between notes updates (1–100).
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.meta_max_: How many tips the notes may hold (1–20).
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.max_paral: How many versions are scored at once (1–8). Higher is faster and puts more load on the scorer.
How many changes the models propose at once (1–8).
tooltip.submit.blackbox.shinka.extra_mod: Add up to four more optimization models. With several models ShinkaEvolve learns which one improves scores most and calls it more often.
tooltip.submit.blackbox.proposer_ralph: AutoResearch rounds: each agent session is one round with a fresh directive, and new rounds start until the optimization budget is spent or progress stalls
